title: Extending Deep Reinforcement Learning Frameworks in Cryptocurrency Market Making

extraction.methodology_summary: Two policy-based deep reinforcement learning algorithms, A2C and PPO, are trained as market-making agents using a multi-layer perceptron neural network. The observation space integrates limit order book data, order flow, imbalances, and hand-crafted indicators across various window sizes. Agents interact with the environment via time-based snapshots or a newly proposed price-based event environment (triggered by midpoint price changes exceeding a threshold), and are evaluated across seven different reward functions.
extraction.universe: Bitcoin perpetual contract (XBTUSD) on Bitmex exchange

performance_metrics.context: Buy-and-hold benchmark strategy over the 30-day out-of-sample period
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: enables the benchmark to generate a 16.25% return during this period.

performance_metrics.context: Best performing A2C agent using Trade Completion TC reward function and feature set 3 in the time-based environment
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: The best result obtained from our agents is a 17.61% return over this same period, using reward function Trade Completion T C, A2C algorithm, and feature combination Set 3 for the observation space.

key_findings: The A2C algorithm outperformed the PPO agent in terms of highest cumulative return and number of profitable experiments.

Defining events based on price changes rather than time intervals made environments easier for agents to learn, yielding more stable trading patterns and less erratic behavior during large price jumps.
Goal-oriented reward functions such as Trade Completion (TC) achieved the highest overall returns in both time- and price-based environments.
Agents utilizing PnL-based rewards without realized gains incorporated tended to exhibit nearsighted trading behavior and incurred frequent transaction cost losses.
limitations: All experiments incurred significant losses ranging between 5% and 10% during a sharp Bitcoin sell-off on January 19, 2020.
The train-test split was selected based on data availability rather than an empirical methodology.
